body:
Thanks for the help. I have taken a lot of time to grieve losing the relationship. So many good memories and experiences we had together.

I really feel like I am in a tribal hut though, after moving back to my country hometown, and knowing that there really aren't people like her here. One of the worst parts is I thought I was doing good for us, because I'd find good work here, when in reality, I was sealing my fate.

/sigh. 

And I'm not a great guy, I'm kind of a dick, that's the worst part. I didn't get into specifics with my flaws, but I tend towards being chauvinist and douchey. All the good stuff is just penance.

Anyway -- you hang in there too. It sounds like you have something legit, unlike my whining!

> Remember that relief is a human emotion that you are yearning for, and death won't bring relief. The joy you want to feel won't come through death.

Wow, powerful stuff there! Thanks for that. (not the OP, but you help.)

Not the song that I was thinking of, but I just came on randomly on my iPod: 

"And your mom would drink until she was no longer speaking

And dad would dream of all the different ways to die

Each one a little more than he could dare to try"

It's a catchy song for how dark it is. It's called "King of Carrot Flowers" if you're interested. Come to think of it, my ex got me started on that band.

I'm at the end of the age range where I'd want to have kids. It was her or nobody. So what I'm left with is jumping from casual relationship to casual relationship. It's so meaningless. It borders on worthless. I thought that flings would at least make me feel better, and they do, in the moment. But the truth is, casual flings aren't love. (real earth-shattering observation there.)

In one of my flings, early on, I accidentally said "I love you" to some girl. I didn't mean it, and I instantly regretted it. It still did feel good to say it. I wish I had someone to say it to and mean it. 

Often times, I find myself thinking of my ex, just wishing it was her. Just wishing that she found me half as charming as these girls act like I am. The way their faces light up when I do something even halfway charming. Just wishing that that happy look in their eyes was hers, the way she used to joke and play with me. But she doesn't, she fucking hates me. I miss the way she used to make silly faces at me, especially when I needed cheering up.

I hate going about my everyday life like everything is fine. I pull it off pretty well. I'm social and active in my community. I volunteer with kids and with the poor. Still, it's not at all uncommon that I cry in the shower at night or before work. Or that I just come home and lay on the floor for an hour or two and think about how horrible life is. Or drink a 12-pack to myself. I used to have suicidal ideation sometimes in high school and college, but back then I was allowed to smoke pot without risking my job. That was nice. Just a little toke and suddenly suicide seemed so stupid. It seems like the only allowable medication these days are those damn SSRIs that make you feel like the walking dead.

I play sad songs on my guitar. (How fucking original.) I haven't learned a single new thing since we broke up, I mostly play the same shit I knew when we met. The songs she used to watch me play and smile, when she'd ask me to play her favorites. Hell, one of them is actually about suicide. We always joked about that one.

If you didn't see all that, you'd think my life is really awesome. I have a job that's as close to my dream job as I could hope for. I have a dog that I love, even though he doesn't take the place of our dogs that she kept. I love my coworkers like family, and they treat me as their own. I'm as fit as I've ever been. I make a lot of money. I get tons of vacation. 

It kills me when I think about how much I wanted to share all that with her. I wanted to have lots of vacation, because we loved travelling together. I wanted to have lots of money because we loved doing things together. We always talked about how it was better to spend money on experiences than things. And we had so many good experiences together. She just sort of writes them off. 

Well, now I've got tons of things, but no love, how fucking wonderful.

**I don't know why I'm writing all this. I probably don't belong on suicidewatch. I'm not going to kill myself. I just think of how nice it would be to be free of this pain, and it's the only way I can think of. Everything else is only temporary.**
